titulo: Sound as a character: native dialogue, voice, score and effects
lead: In 2026 sound stopped being the last step: the main generators return ambience, effects and speech together with the image. This forces you to decide, shot by shot, what is born with the video and what comes in later, like the score and the narration. This lesson settles that decision in a sound map.
objetivo: decide, shot by shot, what is heard and what comes out with the video or separately, and build the scene's sound map.

aprende.t: Split the sound into layers: ambience, effect, line, score and silence
Decide what comes out with the video and what goes in at the edit
Choose score and voice with a clear license and your own voice
Mix with the voice in front and the music underneath

hero_alt: Dark sound studio with the faders of a mixing console in the foreground, a boom microphone with a windscreen and headphones on the desk.

secoes.titulo: The sound layers of a shot
secoes.sub: Five layers. Click each one and see where it usually comes from.

nos.detalhe: Wind, street, a radio in the background. It tells where the scene takes place without showing it. It usually comes out well from the generator, together with the image (native sound).
Door, footsteps, steam, the bread crust crackling. Foley is the effect recorded separately and synced to the image. If the effect has to land on an exact frame, native or recorded in sync.
Short dialogue synced to the mouth: in Oct/2026 the main generators do it in the same pass. Long narration, which runs across several shots, is recorded or synthesized separately.
The music only the audience hears. It runs across shots, so it goes in at the edit, never shot by shot. Under a line, a score without vocals.
Put it all together with a hierarchy: the voice dominates, the music stays underneath, the effect appears at the right moment. Check with headphones at the end.

secoes.legenda: Rule of thumb: what comes from the action of the shot can come out with the video; what crosses shots goes into the edit.

secoes.titulo: How to decide the sound, step by step
secoes.sub: In the scene "The first batch", using the sound column of the shot list from course 0.

texto: Native audio became the standard in 2026 in the main generators (dated examples, Oct/2026: Veo 3.1, Kling 3.0, Seedance 2.x, Runway Gen-4.5). Seedance 2.5 accepts up to 10 reference audios per generation.
Use native for what comes from the shot: ambience, the effect of the action, a short line. Keep separate what crosses shots, what has to sound the same in all of them, and what will change language.

exemplo.texto: Wind and knocks on the door: native. Score and opening narration: separate, in the edit.

passos.sub: what you hear tells you where we are
texto: Diegetic sound exists in the scene and the character hears it; non-diegetic sound only the audience hears, like the score. A well-resolved shot has ambience and the effect of the action.
Silence is a choice too: cut the music before the turning point, leave one shot with only the ambience, a breath after the impact. If you can show it, don't narrate it.

Music generators change fast: Suno released v5.5 on 03/26/2026; a v6 and ElevenLabs' Eleven v3 appear only as reported, not confirmed by an official source. Read each tool's license of use before you publish.
Synthetic or cloned voice: only your own, or from someone who authorized it in writing (lesson 7). Free, local route: Concat cleans and levels the voice and has an AI voice.

passos.sub: the voice is never drowned out
texto: The voice dominates; the music stays atmospheric, underneath; the effect appears at the moment of the action. The most common mistake is leaving the music at the same volume as the voice.
Starting point: lower the score until the line is clear without effort, then check with headphones. Leave a few extra seconds of score for the exit fade.

secoes.sub: The format the page checks, and a request for the AI assistant to draft the map from the shot list.

blocos.conteudo:
Scene: <name> (<duration> s)
Score: <style, where it comes in and where it goes out; with or without vocals>
# n | what you hear | origin
1 | ambience: <...>; effect: <...> | origin: <native or separate>
2 | line: "<short sentence>" | origin: <native or separate>

blocos.rot: Request to the AI assistant (draft of the sound map)

secoes.sub: Paste the file (or upload the .txt). Test first with the example that passes and the example with errors.
secoes.rot: Paste your sound map here (the Trilha line and one numbered line per shot):

termos: ambiente / ambiência / ambient / ambience / room tone / ambient sound / sonido ambiente
efeito / efeitos / foley / sfx / effect / effects / sound effect / sound effects / efecto / efectos
fala / diálogo / dialogue / dialog / line / narração / narration / voz / voice / narración
trilha / música / music / score / soundtrack / banda sonora
nativo / gerado junto / native / generated with the video / generado junto
separado / em separado / pós-produção / separate / post-production / por separado / postproducción / posproducción

secoes.ok: OK: {n} shots with a sound layer and origin decided
secoes.exemplo:
Scene: The first batch (20 s)
Score: slow, quiet piano, no vocals; comes in on shot 4 and rises on 6; fades out in the last second
# n | what you hear | origin
1 | ambience: wind and a dog far away | origin: native
2 | ambience: quiet radio; effect: dough slapping on the counter | origin: native
3 | effect: oven creak and hiss of steam | origin: separate (recorded at the bakery oven)
4 | silence for one second; then effect: the crust crackling | origin: native
5 | effect: three knocks on the iron door; line: "Coming!" | origin: native, short dialogue
6 | score rises; ambience: the street waking up | origin: separate, in the edit
secoes.exemplo_errado:
Cena: A primeira fornada (20 s)
1 | ambiente: vento | origem: nativo
2 | efeito: massa batendo | origem: nativo ou separado
3 | rangido do forno | origem: separado
4 | o pão saindo do forno
5 | fala: "Já vai!" | origem: nativo

exercicios.texto: Write the Trilha line and one line per shot, with what you hear and the origin (nativo or separado). Paste it into "Check your sound map" and download the mapa-som.txt to the project folder.
exercicios.pronto: the page answers OK: [n] planos com camada de som e origem decidida and the mapa-som.txt file is in the project folder.

exercicios.texto: Pick the shot before the turning point of your scene and leave only ambience or silence in it, with no score and no line. Check again.
exercicios.pronto: the page keeps answering OK: … and the shot before the turning point has only ambience or silence in your list.

secoes.sub: Four questions. The explanation appears after each answer.

perguntas.p: The score of your film runs across all six shots. Where should it come from?
opcoes: From each generated shot, with the same music requested in every prompt.
From the generator, in the last shot, which is then copied to the others.
From the edit: it comes in separate, on top of the shots already cut.
From nowhere: score gets in the way of the generators' native sound.
perguntas.explica: What runs across shots goes into the edit. Asking for the same music in six generations gives you six different pieces of music, cut at every shot.

perguntas.p: Which of these layers usually comes out well as native sound, together with the video?
opcoes: The one-minute narration that explains the whole film, from the first shot to the last.
The ambience of the place and the effect of the action in the shot itself.
The score with vocals that plays from start to finish.
The Spanish version of the line, for another market.
perguntas.explica: Ambience and effect come from the action in the shot and sync on their own. Long narration, score and language swaps run across shots or change later: they stay separate.

perguntas.p: Your mix is ready and the line disappears when the score rises. What should you fix?
opcoes: Lower the score under the line and check with headphones until the line is clear.
Raise everything to the maximum so the film feels stronger.
Remove the line and tell the story with the music alone.
Swap the score for a faster one, keeping the same volume as before under the line.
perguntas.explica: Hierarchy: the voice dominates and the music stays underneath. Raising everything causes distortion; swapping the music without lowering the volume repeats the problem.

perguntas.p: You want to use a cloned voice in the narration. Which voice can it be?
opcoes: A famous announcer's, if the video is free.
Anyone's, as long as the film has an AI label.
A well-known movie character's, since it is a tribute.
Yours, or the voice of someone who authorized its use in writing.
perguntas.explica: Voice is a personal trait: cloning someone else's without authorization is imitation, with or without a label and with or without charging for it. Lesson 7 covers image and voice rights.

itens.texto: What comes from the shot goes out with it; what runs across shots goes into the edit.
A shot with only ambience before the turning point gives it weight.
Music underneath, a spot effect, a check with headphones. Cloned voice: only yours or an authorized one.
